extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and readers interested in American literature and poetic craft
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for what constitutes transcendent poetry, the qualities of a national (American) literature, and related virtues of poetic voice and maturity; aimed at assessing or guiding poets and critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature age as source of transcendent poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The rarest and most blessed quality of transcendent noble poetry is, from sane, completed, vital, capable old age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitman argues that highest poetry (like highest law or wisdom) often comes from a matured, completed, vital old age; the poet's accumulated life and physiologic/psychologic continuance produce a unique culminating aura. Example: the perfected bloom or finished wheat-head metaphor—completed fruitage comes in grand age as culmination of preceding life/work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matured, accreted atmosphere as final proof of song
rubrics_metrics.description: The final proof of song or personality is a sort of matured, accreted, superb, evoluted, almost divine, impalpable diffuseness and atmosphere or invisible magnetism—and not any special achievement of passion, pride, metrical form, epigram, plot, thought, or what is call'd beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetry by its overall diffuse, magnetic presence that 'dissolves and embraces all' rather than by isolated technical feats or picturesque elements. The critic should look for an enveloping quality that unites preceding works into a singular aura.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed fruitage / culmination after preceding works
rubrics_metrics.description: Great poetic achievement is like the perfected bloom or finished fruit that stands above earlier stages; it is the culminating aureole of several preceding works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a poet's oeuvre historically; masterpieces often arrive as ripened results of preceding effort. Assess how a work synthesizes and transcends earlier pieces rather than treating single works atomistically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble and diversity as tap-root of national literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble is the tap-root of National Literature; national literature forms slowly from many, deeper mixings and siftings across regions, races, generations—not from two or three dominant influences or any learned syllabus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge emerging national literature by its breadth and plurality: regional voices, class groups, immigrant inputs, and generational continuity. Beware over-centralization (e.g., Atlantic cities claiming to dominate the whole).

rubrics_metrics.name: Autochthonic song / rooted authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: A true national literature must have its autochthonic song—born poetic expression coming from its own soil and soul, its area, spread, idiosyncrasies, returning again like rain distilled from land and sea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that are authentically rooted in local landscapes, customs, speech, and experience rather than mere imitation of foreign fashions. Authenticity is shown by original forms and themes arising from local life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality / Solidarity across humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry must run through entire humanity; the new work should twine all lands like a divine thread and have reference to all—Solidarity being the modern word for this demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether poems, while being locally rooted, still address universal human conditions and connect disparate peoples. National literature should aim for a scope that resonates beyond parochial limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance respect for tradition with devotion to the present
rubrics_metrics.description: The national literatus's task is to treat old hereditaments, legends, poems, theologies, and customs with fitting respect and toleration, and at the same time clearly understand, justify, and exploit our own day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good work neither blindly reveres the past nor discards it; evaluate how a poem/dialogue engages inherited materials while asserting contemporary relevance and original treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine patriotism and nationality, not mere braggadocio
rubrics_metrics.description: What is deepest wanted as roots for literature are Patriotism, Nationality, Ensemble—not mere bawling and braggadocio but radical emotion-facts, fervor, and perennial fructifying spirit at fountain-head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between shallow nationalist rhetoric and deep patriotic feeling that produces sustained, fertile themes. Prize literature that embodies genuine civic/spiritual engagement rather than bombastic slogans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noblesse Oblige / moral responsibility of national literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The spirit of 'Noblesse Oblige' should influence and permeate official America and its representatives and likewise the national literature—implying responsibility and elevated conduct for a developed nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether literature carries a sense of obligation, moral seriousness, and responsibility appropriate to a nation's power and maturity; consider Whitman's exhortation that a 'rich and develop'd nation' should enact this motto practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of moral complexity including 'evil' and criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern poetic quality demands a Deific identity and scope superior to limitations, essentially including so-called evil and crime and criminals—all malformations and defects of the universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works for willingness to include and reckon with moral ambiguity, social outcasts, and the darker aspects of life rather than sanitizing or excluding them; true breadth embraces the full human spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety and trust in the reader (well-hidden allusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The common people relish a well-hidden allusion or hint left faintly indicated and to be disinterr'd or not; it is a capital compliment from author to reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value and reward subtle, suggestive writing that assumes intelligence in readers—small, faint allusions can enhance depth. Avoid over-explication that deprives readers of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding puritanical narrowness; seek philosophic breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Puritanism and its radiations must be respected, but puritanical standards are constipated, narrow, and non-philosophic—insufficient for a vast, varied commonwealth's literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique works that default to narrow moralizing or constrained conventionalism; encourage philosophical, expansive treatment of subjects rather than rectitude alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitality, simple natural health, and first-hand power
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest feature needed is first-class power and simple, natural health, flourishing and produced at first hand—modern verse often lacks the modern and is possessed in spirit with the past; novels and plays can be morbid and effete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer work that feels alive, immediate, and physiologically/psychologically healthy rather than derivative morbidity. Evaluate presence, energy, and organic force in the writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic and spiritual orientation appropriate to the New World
rubrics_metrics.description: The Old World is the region of the poetry of concrete past things; the New World (America) is the region of the future, and its poetry must be spiritual and democratic—evolution applies to verse as to politics and inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether American poetry aspires to democratic inclusiveness and an expanded spirituality fitting modern science and sensibilities, rather than transplanting aristocratic or feudal aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: The human voice (timbre) as central to poetic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The human voice is a cultivation on a fair native foundation; the grand voice is mainly physiological and the quality and power of the right voice (timbre) touches the soul—elocution and vocalization matter deeply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For spoken poetry and performance, evaluate timbre, physiological basis of voice, and vocal cultivation; consider the voice itself as a formative, even elemental, route to poetic impact. Examples: Alboni, Fanny Kemble, Booth cited for vocal power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance across generations as a test of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Every really first-class production must likely pass through the crucial tests of a generation, perhaps several generations; true works endure despite early repulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure works by their capacity to persist and gain recognition over time; initial critical hostility (as with Shakespeare) does not disqualify great originality. Historical evidence: Voltaire and French critics initially disparaged Shakespeare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality that may initially repel critics
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sight of any work really new and first-rate in beauty and originality always arouses something disagreeable and repulsive; people resent anything new as a personal insult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and contextualize early negative responses to radical work; value perseverance and longer-term assessment rather than immediate popularity or critical approbation.
